# The standing at a glance {#sec-standing}

*Before this chapter:* @sec-baselines (the baselines, the reference
configurations and the scoring protocol) and @sec-metrics (the error
metric). The chapters after this one give each row its context.

```{python}
#| label: para-standing-lede
#| output: asis
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
import standing as S
print(f"**On the {len(S.final())} tasks whose standing is final, ISLA at its reference configuration leads on some fields, is "
      "level on others and trails on a few, and on every flow task it is the only one of the three architectures whose error "
      f"does not change when the test geometry is moved, or, on the surface tasks, resampled.** {S.tally_note()} This chapter is the evidence of "
      "Part IV on one page: one table with every headline number, one figure for each of the two invariances, and a reading of "
      "where ISLA leads and trails. Each dataset chapter then opens up its rows. Every row of the table is scored in distribution, "
      "on a dataset that covers one narrow family, so the table measures interpolation within each family. Two datasets test "
      "the generalization to new families that design needs: SHIFT-SUV's estate-trained models scored on fastbacks they never saw, "
      "and AeroZoo's held-out families of bodies and enclosures (@sec-standing-families).")
```

## Every headline number {#sec-standing-table}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-thesis
#| output: asis
out = ["| dataset and task | field | ISLA error | GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA | Transolver ÷ ISLA | ISLA rotated and translated ÷ native | chapter |",
       "|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|"]
for k, f, lab in ROWS:
    s = S.Standing(k)
    cells = []
    for a in S.BASELINES:
        v = s.verdict(a, f)
        word = {"leads": "ISLA leads", "trails": "ISLA trails", "is level with": "level", "is not compared with": "no verdict§"}[v]
        cells.append(f"{S.fmt_ratio(s.ratio(a, f))} ({word})" if s.has(a) else "—")
    name = s.ds.name + (" (trained and tested on estates)" if k == "shift_suv" else "") + (" ‡" if s.in_flight else "")
    out.append(f"| {name} | {s.fields[f]} | {s.err('ISLA', f):.4f} | {cells[0]} | {cells[1]} | {s.shift('ISLA', f, 'posed'):.3f} | @{s.ds.section} |")
print("\n".join(out) + "\n")
KEYS = list(dict.fromkeys(k for k, _, _ in ROWS))
INS = lambda s: ("the " if s.ds.key == "lug" else "") + s.ds.in_sentence
MORE = [(S.Standing(k), a) for k in KEYS for a in S.ARCHS if S.Standing(k).n_seeds(a) != 2]
seed_txt = "Seed means over two seeds" + ("" if not MORE else " (" + "; ".join(
    f"{S._COUNT[s.n_seeds(a)]} for {a} on {s.ds.short}" for s, a in MORE) + ")")
print(": The standing of the three reference configurations on every dataset with a standing artifact: ISLA's "
      "relative L2 error (@sec-metrics) on the native mesh, each baseline's error divided by ISLA's, and ISLA's own error when every test case "
      f"is rotated and translated, over its native error. {seed_txt}, float32, the validation or test split of "
      "each dataset (@sec-splits). The words apply the book's seed rule: a lead needs every seed of one architecture below every "
      "seed of the other and the seed means at least 3% apart. "
      + ("‡: in flight, as the notes below the table say. " if any(S.Standing(k).in_flight for k in KEYS) else "")
      + "How to read this: a "
      "ratio above one favors ISLA; rows are different problems and are not comparable with one another; every baseline reads the "
      "freestream as a unit direction (@tbl-model-inputs). AeroZoo has its own table (@sec-standing-families). Data: "
      "results/char/*_090.json (the artifact of each row is named in its chapter).")
```

## The two invariances, measured {#sec-standing-invariances}

**Move the geometry, and on every flow task only ISLA's error stays put;
redraw a surface task's surface, and again only ISLA's stays put.** Two scorings of every checkpoint test the two properties ISLA is
built for (@sec-invariances). *Rotated and translated* applies a random
rigid motion to every test case, a different one per case, and asks each
model for the field on the moved body. *Uniform point cloud* replaces the
native surface mesh by points drawn uniformly by area, at the same count,
with exact quadrature weights; it changes the scored set itself on the
three surface tasks whose meshes exceed the cell budget (DrivAerML
Surface, HiLiftAeroML, SHIFT-SUV), and changes no model's input anywhere
else. @fig-standing-shifts shows both, each as an architecture's error
under the scoring over its own native error.

```{python}
#| label: fig-standing-shifts
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Each architecture's own error under a changed presentation of the same
#|   test cases, over its native error, on a log scale. Top: every case
#|   rotated and translated, on every dataset. Bottom: the surface redrawn as
#|   a uniform point cloud, on the three surface tasks where that changes the
#|   scored set. ISLA blue squares, ISLA-DTT light open squares (AirfRANS),
#|   GeoTransolver red circles, Transolver amber triangles; the vertical line
#|   is no change. How to read this: these are changes of each model's own
#|   error, not comparisons between models; a baseline mark at 20 means its
#|   error is twenty times its native error. ISLA's one mark away from one is
#|   the lug's; nodes of the lug that lie equally close to two surface
#|   features of the exact geometry are a candidate cause, not isolated
#|   (@sec-lug). Data: results/char/*_090.json.
#| fig-height: 6.4
#| code-fold: true
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8, 6.2), gridspec_kw=dict(hspace=0.35, height_ratios=[2.6, 1.0]))
for ax, protocol, lim in ((axes[0], "posed", (0.8, 900)), (axes[1], "area", (0.8, 20))):
    S.plot_shifts(ax, protocol)
    ax.set_xlim(*lim)
    ticks = [t for t in (1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500) if lim[0] <= t <= lim[1]]
    ax.set_xticks(ticks); ax.set_xticklabels([str(t) for t in ticks]); ax.minorticks_off()
axes[0].set_xlabel("rotated and translated ÷ native, own error [–]")
axes[1].set_xlabel("uniform point cloud ÷ native, own error [–]")
label_line(axes[0], 1.12, 7.3, "ISLA", BLUE, fontsize=8.5)
label_line(axes[0], 60, 7.3, "GeoTransolver", RED, fontsize=8.5, ha="center")
label_line(axes[0], 60, 6.55, "Transolver", AMBER, fontsize=8.5, ha="center")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: para-standing-invariances
#| output: asis
SOLIDS = ("tensile2d", "lug", "deepjeb")
FLOW = [k for k in S.final() if k not in SOLIDS]
SURF = [k for k in S.final() if "area" in S.DATASETS[k].protocols]
VOL = S.Standing("drivaerml_volume")
sh = lambda ks, archs, p: [S.Standing(k).shift(a, f, p) for k in ks for f in S.DATASETS[k].headline for a in archs]
ip = max(abs(x - 1) for x in sh(FLOW, ["ISLA"], "posed"))
bp = sh(FLOW, S.BASELINES, "posed")
ia = max(abs(x - 1) for x in sh(SURF, ["ISLA"], "area"))
ba = sh(SURF, S.BASELINES, "area")
print(f"Over every headline field of the {len(FLOW)} flow tasks, the rigid motion leaves ISLA's error within {100 * ip:.1f}% of its native value and "
      f"multiplies the baselines' by {min(bp):.0f} to {max(bp):.0f}: rotated, a model that reads coordinates is asked about a "
      f"pose it has never seen, and it answers with something worse than the mean field. {S.tally_note()} On the three surface tasks, every field, the uniform "
      f"point cloud moves ISLA's error by at most {100 * ia:.1f}% and multiplies the baselines' by {min(ba):.1f} to {max(ba):.1f}: "
      "a model that averages over points rather than over area answers a different question when the points move. "
      f"On the DrivAerML Volume task the uniform point cloud is left out: {VOL.degenerate['area']}. What exact re-meshing "
      "of that task's boundary does to ISLA is measured in @sec-interior-boundary-law.")
LUG = S.Standing("lug")
SOL = [k for k in S.final() if k in SOLIDS]
is_ = max(abs(x - 1) for x in sh(SOL, ["ISLA"], "posed"))
bs_ = sh(SOL, S.BASELINES, "posed")
print()
print(f"On {' and '.join(S.DATASETS[k].short for k in SOL)} the rigid motion multiplies the baselines' errors by {min(bs_):.1f} "
      f"to {max(bs_):.0f} and leaves ISLA's within {100 * is_:.2f}%. On the lug it multiplies ISLA's von Mises error by "
      f"{LUG.shift('ISLA', 'von_mises_l2', 'posed'):.2f}, on the in-flight rows (@tbl-thesis).")
```

## Where ISLA leads, where it is level, where it trails {#sec-standing-reading}

```{python}
#| label: para-standing-groups
#| output: asis
GROUPS = (("External aerodynamics, surface fields", ("drivaerml_surface", "shift_suv", "hilift")),
          ("Flow fields in the volume", ("drivaerml_volume", "airfrans")),
          ("Solid mechanics", ("lug", "deepjeb", "tensile2d")))
def reading(k):
    s = S.Standing(k)
    parts = []
    for word, label in (("leads", "ISLA leads"), ("is level with", "is level"), ("trails", "trails")):
        items = [f"{s.fields[f]} against {a} ({S.fmt_ratio(s.ratio(a, f))})" for f in s.ds.headline for a in S.BASELINES
                 if s.has(a) and s.verdict(a, f) == word]
        if items:
            parts.append(f"{label} on " + ", ".join(items))
    held = "".join(f"; its {s.fields[f]} ratios are given without a verdict, because {why}" for f, why in s.ds.provisional.items())
    n = s.n_seeds("ISLA")
    if n > 2:
        held += "; ISLA's " + S._COUNT[n] + " seeds span " + ", ".join(
            f"{min(s.seeds('ISLA', f)):.4f} to {max(s.seeds('ISLA', f)):.4f} on {s.fields[f]}" for f in s.ds.headline)
    name = INS(s) + (", trained and tested on estates," if k == "shift_suv" else "")
    rows = ", on the in-flight rows (@tbl-thesis, " if s.in_flight else " ("
    return f"On {name} ISLA " + "; ".join(p.replace("ISLA leads", "leads") for p in parts) + held + f"{rows}@{s.ds.section})"
for title, keys in GROUPS:
    txt = ". ".join(reading(k) for k in keys if k in S.available())
    if title == "Solid mechanics":
        txt += (". On the lug, ISLA reads which faces are clamped, which is the hole, which half of it is loaded and the pressure "
                "on it; GeoTransolver reads the same four labels on the surface triangles, and Transolver reads none (@sec-interior-lug)")
    print(f"**{title}.** {txt}.\n")
```

## What the standing compares, and what it does not {#sec-standing-scope}

**Each architecture runs at a configuration that trains under one memory
ceiling, so the comparison is matched in memory, not in parameters.** The
three reference configurations come from candidates that train under
80 GiB per GPU on two selection datasets, the DrivAerML Surface task and
HiLiftAeroML at 510 training cases; the registered selection rule named no
single configuration for both datasets, and each pick has the smallest joint score over the two
(@sec-selection). No architecture's pick, ISLA's included, is its most
accurate candidate on the car, and for the baselines the wing scores that
decided it are scores under the freestream in inch/s (@sec-selection). The three spend their
memory differently, as @tbl-standing-cost shows: at similar memory, ISLA
has several times GeoTransolver's parameters.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-standing-cost
#| output: asis
import json, re
COST_RAW = json.load(open(S.CHAR / S.COST_FILE))
# the eager-trained lanes are the AirfRANS, Tensile2d and lug ISLA standings, not a control alone
COST_NOTE = re.sub(r" \([a-z0-9_*]+\)", "", COST_RAW["note"]).replace("they trained eager only for the training-path control, at", "they train at")
CKEYS = [k for k in S.available() + ["aerozoo"] if S.cost(k, "ISLA")]
and_ = lambda xs: ", ".join(xs[:-1]) + " and " + xs[-1] if len(xs) > 1 else "".join(xs)
BEFORE = [S.DATASETS[k].short for k in CKEYS if "before the compile fix" in S.cost(k, "ISLA")["note"]]
FIXED = [S.DATASETS[k].short for k in CKEYS if "r090fix_" in S.cost(k, "ISLA")["source"]]
TIMED = [S.DATASETS[k].short for k in COST_RAW["compiled_before_fix"]]
FIXMOVE = max(abs(S.cost(k, a)["step_seconds"] / c["step_seconds"] - 1)
              for k, v in COST_RAW["compiled_before_fix"].items() for a, c in v.items())
CARCHS = ("ISLA", "ISLA-DTT") + S.BASELINES
# a cell's reason, from its note: the clause that names the smoke lane, without run identifiers or step counts
why = lambda c, word: re.sub(r" \([a-z0-9_]+\)|, \d[\d,]* steps", "", next(p for p in c["note"].split("; ") if word in p))
FLAGS = {"¹": lambda c: "smoke lane" in c["note"], "‡": lambda c: "in flight" in c["note"],
         "²": lambda c: c["precision"] != "bfloat16"}
flag = lambda c: "".join(f for f, test in FLAGS.items() if test(c))
marked = {f: [] for f in FLAGS}
out = ["| dataset and task | | " + " | ".join(CARCHS) + " |", "|---|---|" + "---:|" * len(CARCHS)]
for k in CKEYS:
    c = {a: S.cost(k, a) for a in CARCHS}
    if not all(c[a] for a in S.ARCHS):
        continue
    for a in CARCHS:
        for f in flag(c[a]) if c[a] else "":
            marked[f].append((k, a, c[a]))
    cells = lambda fmt: " | ".join(fmt(c[a]) + flag(c[a]) if c[a] else "—" for a in CARCHS)
    out.append(f"| {S.DATASETS[k].name} | parameters [millions] | " + cells(lambda x: f"{x['n_parameters'] / 1e6:.1f}") + " |")
    out.append("| | training peak memory [GiB per GPU] | " + cells(lambda x: f"{x['peak_gib']:.0f}") + " |")
    out.append("| | training step [s] | " + cells(lambda x: f"{x['step_seconds']:.2f}") + " |")
print("\n".join(out) + "\n")
print(": The resources of the reference configurations on each task, from the training logs of the standing's own lanes: "
      "trainable parameters, the training peak device memory per GPU (the maximum over the ranks) and the median training step, "
      "leaving out the compile steps, seed means; AeroZoo's lanes are those of its `full` split, and its Transolver is AeroZoo's "
      f"own configuration, {ARM['Transolver']}. {COST_NOTE} "
      f"On {and_(FIXED)} the ISLA rows are the lanes trained on the compiled path with the mix-order setting, not the "
      "eagerly trained lanes behind the standing. "
      f"ISLA's lanes on {and_(BEFORE)} trained before the mix-order setting; where both were "
      f"timed, on {and_(TIMED)}, the setting moves the median step by at most {100 * FIXMOVE:.1f}%. "
      + (f"¹ {and_([f'{S.DATASETS[k].short} {a}' for k, a, _ in marked['¹']])}: "
         + "; ".join(sorted({why(c, "smoke lane") for *_, c in marked["¹"]})) + ". " if marked["¹"] else "")
      + (f"‡ {and_([f'{S.DATASETS[k].short} {a}' for k, a, _ in marked['‡']])}: the lane is still training, "
         "priced on the epochs logged so far. " if marked["‡"] else "")
      + (f"² {and_([f'{S.DATASETS[k].short} {a}' for k, a, _ in marked['²']])}: trained in float32, as logged. "
         if marked["²"] else "")
      + "How to read this: the three architectures are matched by the memory ceiling of the selection rule, not by parameter "
      "count; ISLA has several times GeoTransolver's parameters at similar memory; a step trains on one case per rank. "
      f"Data: results/char/{S.COST_FILE}.")
```

The standing is a statement about these three configurations on these
splits with the seeds of @tbl-thesis. It does not say that ISLA would lead
at equal parameter count, nor how the comparison moves with the training
set's size (@sec-capacity has the scaling evidence, on smaller ISLA
configurations). On AeroZoo it says nothing about pressure against a
baseline that has learned pressure (@tbl-standing-aerozoo). Every scope
statement is collected in @sec-limits.
